description:
You are a psychology professor setting up an online replication of the classic Tversky & Kahneman (1981) framing effect experiment using LimeSurvey. The experiment presents multiple decision scenarios, and the ORDER in which scenarios appear must be randomized across participants to control for order effects.

Log in to LimeSurvey (Username: admin, Password: Admin123!) and complete the following:

1. Create a new survey titled: 'Framing Effect Experiment - Cognitive Decision Making Study 2024'

2. Create exactly 5 question groups in this order:
   - 'Informed Consent and Instructions' (always shown first — NO randomization)
   - 'Scenario A - Disease Outbreak' (randomized)
   - 'Scenario B - Financial Decision' (randomized)
   - 'Scenario C - Environmental Policy' (randomized)
   - 'Demographics and Debrief' (always shown last — NO randomization)

3. Set the RANDOMIZATION GROUP for the three Scenario groups (A, B, C) to the value: experimental
   This is found in each group's settings. All three must share the same randomization group name so LimeSurvey randomizes their presentation order. The 'Informed Consent' and 'Demographics' groups must NOT have any randomization group set.

4. Add at least one question to EACH of the 5 groups:
   - Consent group: A Yes/No consent question (e.g., 'Do you consent to participate?')
   - Scenario A: Present the disease outbreak scenario — 'Imagine an unusual disease is expected to kill 600 people' — with two program options (Program A: 200 saved; Program B: 1/3 chance all saved)
   - Scenario B: Present the financial decision — 'A company faces difficulties, 60 employees may lose jobs' — with two plan options
   - Scenario C: Present the environmental policy — 'A coastal city faces flooding, 1200 homes at risk' — with two options
   - Demographics: At least one demographics question (e.g., age)

5. Configure survey settings:
   - DISABLE backward navigation (participants cannot return to previous pages — critical for experimental validity)
   - ENABLE anonymized responses

6. ACTIVATE the survey

The LimeSurvey admin panel is already open in Firefox at http://localhost/index.php/admin
